name: Petersburg National Battlefield
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Petersburg National Battlefield in Virginia preserves the sites associated with the Siege of Petersburg, a nine-month campaign from June 1864 to April 1865 that ultimately led to the end of the Civil War. General Ulysses S. Grant's strategy to cut the vital railroad supply lines feeding the Confederate capital at Richmond resulted in one of the war's longest sustained operations, with miles of trenches foreshadowing the trench warfare of World War I. The siege included the Battle of the Crater on July 30, 1864, in which Union forces detonated a mine beneath Confederate lines — an assault that ended in a disastrous Union defeat and particularly heavy casualties among United States Colored Troops. The fall of Petersburg on April 2, 1865, led directly to the evacuation of Richmond and Lee's surrender at Appomattox a week later.
